A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CALICO method and MIXEDPARTS study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MIXEDPARTS benchmark results, component and layer-injection ablations, computational efficiency measurements, and frequency-stratified performance analysis.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark comparisons, expanded component ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative contextual comparisons.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 retain the same EVA-CLIP/Q-Former architecture, DINOv2-based CEM, CAM injections at layers 11 and 22, segmentation outputs, and combined text/focal/DICE objective. Additional initialization and alignment information does not establish a newly introduced method component.

E1.justification: The three MIXEDPARTS source datasets and common-object, common-part, and unique-part tasks remain. v2 additionally documents training alignment on 3.2M GranD samples in Appendix C.1, extending reported training-data coverage; the PDFs do not establish whether this alignment was already performed in v1.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 5 add two evaluated comparators: Cascade, combining Sparkles, GPT-4o, and LISA, and Multi-Image PartGLEE. VLPart, GLaMM, and LISA remain. This substantially broadens comparison beyond the original three baselines to include a modular pipeline and another part-segmentation foundation model.

E3.justification: The reported CALICO/GLaMM initialization changes from GLaMM FullScope to GranD-pretrained weights, LISA's checkpoint changes from the explanatory variant to LISA-7B-v1, and CALICO's learning rate changes from 3e-4 to 4e-4. v2 also adds per-task inference-time evaluation. These are material setting changes, although they do not independently establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds Q-Former and DINOv2 removal ablations to the existing CEM/CAM study and adds a contextual object-selection case study in Figure 7. Conversely, v1's Appendix E.3 and Figure 7 frequency-stratified robustness analysis disappear. The retained dataset-frequency charts do not replace that performance analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Additional result rows do not change this reporting practice.

E6.justification: Overall, per-task, and ablation results are extensively replaced: Table 1 reports CALICO recall of 50.5 in v1 versus 59.7 in v2, and semantic similarity of 76.5 versus 82.7. Two CAM injections now lead the text metrics, replacing v1's three-injection advantage there. Efficiency values and dataset statistics also change. Revised settings prevent treating these as controlled performance gains.

T1.justification: The formal task definition, architectural equations, losses, and Semantic IoU definition retain their mathematical substance. Loss-equation reformatting and correction of the Ltest label to Ltext do not introduce new theory or reasoning.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same core contributions: the new task, CALICO, MIXEDPARTS, and baseline evaluation, with claims of parameter-efficient and superior co-segmentation. Updated performance margins change supporting results. The more prominent efficiency argument was already present in v1 Appendix E.1.

C2.justification: New Appendices E–F identify concrete limitations involving visually similar parts with different functions and unobserved material properties. v2 also interprets the added ablations and contextual examples, narrows the discussion of CAM removal toward labeling performance, and drops the frequency-robustness interpretation. These extend and qualify the existing account without replacing its central explanation.

D1.justification: Appendix C substantially expands reproducibility information: Q-Former initialization, GranD alignment, LoRA query/value targets, warmup, scheduling, gradient accumulation, specific baseline checkpoints, and the FLOPS profiler. Figure 10 supplies Cascade prompt templates. These are newly documented details; their disclosure alone does not establish that the corresponding procedures were newly introduced.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to PartGLEE, InstructBLIP, the GPT-4 technical report, and ACCESS, and revises descriptions of Semantic-SAM and VLPart. The central positioning against single-image segmentation and unlabeled part co-segmentation remains. Publication updates to existing references are not new cited works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and experimental discussion undergo extensive rewriting. Baseline descriptions move into Appendix C, PartImageNet modifications move from Appendix D to A.2, and dedicated limitations, broader-impact, and attribution sections reorganize the supplement.

P2.justification: v2 adds an efficiency plot, contextual comparison figure, timing table, and Cascade prompt display. Component ablations change from a chart to an expanded table, while layer-injection results change from a table to a chart. Qualitative examples and dataset-chart styling are revised, and the frequency-performance plot is removed.

improvement.justification: Added comparators and targeted Q-Former/DINOv2 ablations strengthen assessment of the retained method, while expanded training documentation and concrete limitations improve reproducibility and interpretation. The gain is moderated by removal of the frequency-stratified robustness analysis. Revised scores under changed settings do not themselves demonstrate better paper quality, but the clearer documentation and broader validation provide an evidence-supported net improvement.
